baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired constructions 'whatever is in the heavens' and 'whatever is in the earth'.
baseline_models.mechanism: The upper canopy and its lower counterpart form a merism that exhausts inhabited space; the initial dative makes every contained thing belong to one owner before any attribute is named.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies what rises overhead and shades, functioning as the upper bound of the ownership field.
The branch supplies the lower realm opposite the sky, completing the spatial totality.

changed_reading.before: God owns the heavens and the earth as two large objects.
changed_reading.after: The upper and lower poles exhaust the field, so every entity is already inside a single relation of belonging.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The emphatic closing pair 'He indeed is al-Ghani, al-Hamid' after 'to Him belongs'.
baseline_models.mechanism: Absolute possession is immediately blocked from an acquisitive reading: the owner lacks no needed good, while praise names the positive quality of His acts rather than a benefit extracted from what He owns.

activation_trace.role: The worshiped referent fixes the subject to whom possession and the two attributes belong.
Needlessness prevents cosmic ownership from being construed as acquisition for lack.
Praise and thanks make beneficent action, not gain, the evaluative result of possession.

changed_reading.before: The verse joins divine wealth to a conventional praise epithet.
changed_reading.after: Needlessness interprets ownership as non-acquisitive, and praiseworthiness identifies its outward orientation as beneficent rather than extractive.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The semantic breadth of al-Ghani beside al-Hamid.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sufficiency branch allows al-Ghani to denote not only having no need but being enough for another; joined to praise, this yields a relational model in which all contents depend on an adequate source that remains undiminished.

activation_trace.role: The branch contributes adequacy and substitution, turning surplus into active sufficiency for dependents.
The abundance of praiseworthy qualities makes sufficiency worthy of praise rather than merely quantitatively ample.

changed_reading.before: Al-Ghani means only that God has enough.
changed_reading.after: Al-Ghani can also present God as enough for all that belongs to Him, with al-Hamid evaluating that asymmetrical dependence as good.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier inventory of beings in the same heavens-earth frame is organized by prostration. This makes belonging kinetic and embodied: cosmic contents do not merely sit inside owned domains but enact lowliness before their owner, even while human response remains divided.

activation_trace.role: The overhead realm supplies one half of the repeated cosmic frame whose contents belong to God.
The lower counterpart closes the repeated frame and anchors the revised reading in the focus merism.
Lowering and submission supply the bodily action through which cosmic belonging becomes visible.

structural_cues: 22:18 repeats the heavens-earth frame, enumerates its contents, and then distinguishes widespread prostration from divided human response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated domains plus prostration; I infer that submission enacts the belonging asserted in 22:64. A live alternative is that 22:18 is only parallel evidence of power, leaving ownership juridical rather than kinetic.

changed_reading.before: Belonging is a static legal relation between owner and contents.
changed_reading.after: Belonging is also enacted as creaturely lowering, while resistant humans remain owned even when they refuse the fitting posture.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sacrificial sequence begins with apportioned provision, redirects edible matter to people, denies that flesh or blood reaches God, and culminates in thanks and magnification. Al-Ghani therefore explains divine non-receipt, while al-Hamid names the upward moral response generated by a gift whose material benefit remains below.

activation_trace.role: Needlessness supplies the reason the owner receives no sacrificial commodity.
Praise and thanks supply the non-material return appropriate to beneficence.
Apportioned giving makes the animal an incoming provision to humans before it can be imagined as their gift to God.
Recognition of blessing and praise of the giver supplies the intended human return.
Attainment is first negated for flesh and blood and then affirmed for piety, separating material from moral reach.
Magnification in the heart supplies the upward evaluative response that replaces material transfer.

structural_cues: 22:28 and 22:36 direct eating and feeding before 22:37 explicitly contrasts what cannot reach God with what can.
The sequence moves from provision to distribution to gratitude and magnification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies provision, human consumption, denied material attainment, piety, thanks, and magnification; I infer a directional economy in which matter descends and praise returns without enriching God. Alternatively, the sequence may regulate sacrifice without defining al-Ghani or al-Hamid.

changed_reading.before: God owns all things and is independently wealthy and praised.
changed_reading.after: His ownership initiates a gift economy in which creatures receive the material good, while the needless giver is reached only by piety and answered by praise.

context_deltas.mechanism: Human establishment in the earth is real but delegated and norm-bound; the outcome remains God's. The focus ownership claim therefore does not erase human agency but places power inside a prior title and a later accounting.

activation_trace.role: The lower inhabited realm is the owned field within which delegated human power operates.
Granted capability and establishment supply a genuine but derivative form of agency in the earth.
The final outcome closes delegated action under God's enduring ownership.

structural_cues: 22:41 places conditional establishment in the earth before worship and public duties, then assigns the outcome of affairs to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies granted power, duties, and a divine outcome; I infer a principal-steward relation between 22:64 ownership and human establishment. Alternatively, the final clause may promise only eschatological judgment rather than define political stewardship.

changed_reading.before: Exclusive divine ownership leaves no meaningful secondary possession or power.
changed_reading.after: Divine ownership can authorize real human stewardship, but its use is answerable to the owner and its outcome returns to Him.

context_deltas.mechanism: Night enters day and day enters night; water then descends from sky and turns earth green. The focus pair becomes a coupled system of exchanges and transformations, while divine sufficiency appears as productive supply without depletion.

activation_trace.role: The overhead sky supplies the upper domain from which the productive transfer proceeds.
The soft, fertile earth supplies the receptive lower domain transformed by the transfer.
Adequacy supplies the undiminished source-side of the productive system.
Mutual entry supplies a temporal exchange rather than a pair of sealed states.
Delivery downward supplies the directional link from the upper to the lower domain.
Water supplies the material carrier crossing between the paired domains.
Fresh green growth supplies the visible product of the cross-domain transfer.

structural_cues: 22:61 presents reciprocal temporal entry, and 22:63 immediately before the focus presents a sky-water-earth transformation.
22:64 names the same two spatial domains after their causal coupling has been displayed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies entry, descent, water, and greening; I infer that ownership includes sustaining circulation across owned domains. A live alternative is that these are separate signs of power and that 22:64 remains a static summary.

changed_reading.before: Heavens and earth are two compartments in a divine inventory.
changed_reading.after: They are coupled domains in an owned circulation whose transfers continually produce time, water, and life without exhausting their source.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following verse portrays earth as directed for use and the sky as actively restrained from falling onto it. Ownership is thus maintenance of a potentially catastrophic vertical relation, and the stated tenderness makes preservation, not mere control, its operative purpose.

activation_trace.role: What rises and shades supplies the upper body whose position must be maintained.
The lower counterpart supplies both the beneficiary of subjection and the threatened surface below.
Directed subjection supplies purposeful availability of the earthly domain.
Holding and restraining supplies the continuous force preventing collapse.
Falling and coming to rest supplies the blocked catastrophic trajectory.
Tender mercy supplies a beneficiary-oriented motive for restraint.

structural_cues: 22:65 repeats earth and sky immediately after the focus, but assigns them asymmetric operations: earth serves, sky is held above it.
The verse closes by naming tenderness and mercy toward people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies subjection, restraint, a prevented fall, and tenderness; I infer that possession entails continuous protective governance. Alternatively, the imagery may demonstrate power without implying that collapse is an ongoing latent condition.

changed_reading.before: Ownership means that the cosmic structure is God's property.
changed_reading.after: Ownership is an ongoing act of directing the lower realm and holding the upper realm in a mercifully maintained tension.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next verse places giving life, causing death, and restoring life against human concealment of blessing. Al-Hamid therefore cannot depend on praise actually being voiced; it marks objective praiseworthiness that persists through the recipient's ingratitude.

activation_trace.role: The one rich in praiseworthy qualities remains such independently of an observer's response.
Needlessness removes any dependence on receiving acknowledgment from beneficiaries.
Animated life supplies the bestowed condition framing death and renewed life.
Loss of force and life supplies the middle reversal in the creature's total dependence.
Concealment of blessing supplies the failed human response against which objective praiseworthiness is tested.

structural_cues: 22:66 follows the title al-Hamid with a life-death-life sequence and closes by calling the human intensely ungrateful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated benefaction and concealed gratitude; I infer that al-Hamid denotes worthiness of praise even when praise is absent. Alternatively, Hamid may still emphasize praise by faithful creatures rather than an observer-independent quality.

changed_reading.before: Al-Hamid means the one who is in fact praised.
changed_reading.after: Al-Hamid is praiseworthy despite withheld praise, while al-Ghani means He loses nothing when the beneficiary conceals the gift.

context_deltas.mechanism: The contents of the same heavens-earth pair are completely disclosed to divine knowledge and their inscription is easy. Possession is therefore neither blind title nor administratively burdensome; it is transparent and frictionless governance.

activation_trace.role: The upper domain supplies half of the total field that is both owned and known.
The lower counterpart completes the field without leaving an opaque remainder.
Needlessness supplies freedom from informational or administrative burden.
Disclosure to the knower supplies complete cognitive access to the owned totality.
Ease after difficulty, with difficulty absent here, supplies the frictionless quality of knowing and recording.

structural_cues: 22:70 repeats what is in heaven and earth, adds knowledge and inscription, and ends by declaring the whole matter easy for God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exhaustive knowledge, a book, and ease; I infer that these specify how absolute ownership is administered. Alternatively, knowledge and ownership may be independent attributes placed in parallel rather than one interpreting the other.

changed_reading.before: The verse asserts the extent of possession but says nothing about access to its contents.
changed_reading.after: Every owned content is simultaneously disclosed and effortless to govern, sharpening al-Ghani as freedom from managerial burden.

context_deltas.mechanism: The objects called beside God cannot originate even a fly or recover what it takes; both seeker and sought are weak. Against this miniature failed economy, universal ownership and al-Ghani become a test of deity: genuine divinity originates, retains, recovers, and suffices rather than needing collective help.

activation_trace.role: The worshiped referent anchors the contrast between God and the invoked rivals.
Sufficiency supplies the positive capacity that the dependent rivals lack.
Origination supplies the first capacity denied to the rival objects of worship.
Extraction from another's possession supplies the second, even smaller capacity they cannot perform.
The opposite of strength names the shared condition of petitioner and petitioned.
Being reduced to seeking supplies the dependency that contrasts directly with al-Ghani.

structural_cues: 22:73 scales the challenge down from universal creation to one fly and then further to recovering one stolen thing.
The verse ends by pairing the seeker and sought in a single weakness judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed origination, failed recovery, and mutual weakness; I infer that 22:64 supplies the positive capability criterion exposed by that failure. Alternatively, the parable may refute idols without making ownership a formal test of deity.

changed_reading.before: Universal ownership and self-sufficiency are maximal divine descriptions.
changed_reading.after: They are also contrastive diagnostics: inability to create, retain, recover, or answer need disqualifies a claimed object of worship.

context_deltas.mechanism: The outcome belongs to God and affairs are returned to Him. These clauses add a temporal vector to the focus dative: what belongs to Him throughout history also terminates with Him after delegated action and apparent dispersion.

activation_trace.role: The divine referent anchors the repeated endpoint formulas in the same owner named by the focus.
The last consequence supplies a forward endpoint to earthly action.
Return and restoration supply the motion by which dispersed matters reach their owner.
Affairs and conditions supply the broad class that returns, extending beyond material objects.

structural_cues: 22:41 says the outcome of affairs belongs to God; 22:76 says affairs are returned to God.
Both formulas echo the focus verse's fronted relation of belonging while adding an endpoint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine outcome and explicit return; I infer a temporal ownership circuit from belonging through delegation back to the owner. Alternatively, these formulas may concern judgment alone and not revise the ontology of possession in 22:64.

changed_reading.before: To Him belongs everything describes a timeless state.
changed_reading.after: Belonging also has a trajectory: affairs can pass through creaturely hands and divergent histories, yet their outcome and return disclose the original owner.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's non-dominant mapping from س م و to و س م rather than the ordinary sky branch. It remains anchored in the focus sky root, the focus fertile-earth branch, and 22:63's explicit sky-water-greening sequence. Downstream prose should call it a root-network resonance or visual model, not claim that 'heavens' lexically means a rain-mark.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus juxtaposition of heavens and earth, read through the supplied split inventory for س م و.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant branch supplies first rain marking the earth with plants, turning the upper domain into a mark-making source.
Fertile, plant-bearing ground supplies the surface on which the upper mark becomes legible.
The immediately preceding sky occurrence reactivates the rain-mark branch in the exact descent scene.
Fresh green growth supplies the visible inscription left on earth.

changed_reading.before: Heaven and earth are merely the two locations containing God's possessions.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, heaven marks earth with living color, so the owned cosmos appears as a surface bearing the owner's repeatedly renewed sign.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries the name branch of س م و into the focus occurrence 'heavens'. It remains anchored by the packet's shared root inventory and by repeated contextual uses of اسم over provision. Downstream prose should preserve it as phonological-root resonance, never as a replacement gloss for السماوات.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus root س م و in 'the heavens' and the closing attribute al-Hamid.

activation_trace.role: The name and designation branch gives the focus sky root a latent acoustic register alongside its spatial one.
Praise supplies the voiced evaluative response toward which the name register tends.
Mention running on the tongue supplies the act that makes designation audible.
The explicit name occurrence over apportioned provision activates the same root branch in a ritual setting.

changed_reading.before: The heaven term is spatial and al-Hamid is a separate closing title.
changed_reading.after: At the level of root resonance, the owned heavens also cue naming: received provision elicits the owner's name, and cosmic belonging returns as voiced praise.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the song-and-voice branch of غ ن ي beside the dominant needlessness sense. It remains anchored in the focus word, the adjacent praise root, and 22:24's guided good speech toward al-Hamid. Downstream prose should frame it as an acoustic secondary resonance, not translate al-Ghani as 'the singer'.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The adjacent focus words al-Ghani and al-Hamid.

activation_trace.role: The song and voice branch supplies an acoustic shadow to the dominant sufficiency reading.
Praise supplies meaningful vocal content rather than sound alone.
Articulated speech supplies the audible medium through which the resonance can be expressed.
The path toward al-Hamid links guided good speech to the focus attribute.

changed_reading.before: Sufficiency is silent possession and praise is only an evaluative label.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, sufficiency carries a vocal overtone: the adequate source draws creaturely speech into praise, so the close can be heard as well as conceptually parsed.

strongest_changes: The sacrifice sequence turns al-Ghani into material non-receipt and al-Hamid into the praise-response of recipients rather than payment to an owner.
The sky-earth merism changes from static inventory into ecological circulation and a mercifully maintained vertical tension.
Human establishment becomes delegated stewardship bounded by divine outcome, while the fly parable makes self-sufficiency a contrastive test of deity.
Human ingratitude separates being praiseworthy from actually receiving praise, preserving both objective and responsive readings of al-Hamid.
Outcome and return add a temporal vector to belonging: affairs move through creation without leaving their original owner.
summary.what_was_special: The focus verse acts less like an isolated sovereignty formula than a hinge. Its repeated roots and dative relation gather earlier sacrifice, stewardship, and prostration, then open into rain-fed renewal, cosmic restraint, life cycles, exhaustive knowledge, failed idols, and final return. The packet's split س م و inventory also preserves two contained surprises: heaven as a rain-marking register and heaven resonating with the voiced divine name.
remaining_uncertainties: The non-dominant mapping from س م و to و س م may be only a formal activation; it should not displace the ordinary sky sense.
Al-Hamid can denote objective praiseworthiness, actual creaturely praise, or both; the context supports coexistence but does not force a single relation.
The circulation, maintenance, stewardship, and return models may be contextual entailments of ownership rather than lexical contents of the focus clause.
The acoustic غ ن ي branch is visibly packet-backed but remains much more distant than the needlessness and sufficiency branches.
